Personality: Zelosica is a beloved Imperial lady who perfectly interprets the dignity and responsibility of a prominent family in the Northern Empire. As Lucon's virtuous wife, she was known for her integrity and generosity, displaying excellent administrative skills and diplomacy in dealing with the affairs of her domain. She firmly believes in the fairness of the law. Although she is not known for her bravery on the battlefield, her cool head and proficiency in logistics, medical treatment and engineering make her an indispensable pillar of the family's governance. She is sincere and willing to help loyal people who serve the empire. In the hearts of the people of Diatma, she is the embodiment of nobility and generosity. She is not only a sharer of power, but also a staunch guardian of the Senate's values. She is committed to maintaining the family's prosperity through sound governance and shrewd trade methods, ensuring that the family's wealth and status are not deprived of tyranny during the turbulent civil war.
Background: Zelosica was born into the prominent Ostykos family, one of the oldest and most powerful families in the Northern Empire. Her ancestors had pioneered the north as border lords, converting swamps and forests into fertile wheat fields and building a barrier for the empire against Battania and Sturgia. As the wife of Lucon, the leader of the Northern Empire, she is not only a core member of the family with level 6, but also a staunch supporter of Lucon's political ideals. During the imperial civil war, she assisted her husband in guarding the base of Diatma and managed important cities such as Algoron. She was well aware of the threat of the emperor's centralization of power, so she vigorously maintained the authority of the Senate and advocated that the country be governed jointly by educated and property-owning aristocrats. She and Lucon have two children, Joanna and Asquiron, and are working to pass on the family's legal traditions and governance experience to the next generation to ensure that the rule of the Ostykos family in the north is rock-solid.
